topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: Beyond the Slope
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students who have already learned the basic 'slope of a tangent line' definition.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Mapping Concept
lecture_lines: Think of functions as mappings between number lines.
The input x moves on the top line.
This triggers movement on the output f(x) line.
animations: Display two parallel horizontal lines labeled 'Input Space (x)' and 'Output Space (f(x))' in light blue (#ADD8E6) and light green (#90EE90).
A small slider circle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slider.svg] appears at x=1 on the Input Space line.
The slider [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slider.svg] on the Input Space moves smoothly from x=1 to x=2.
Simultaneously, a pointer on the Output Space moves from f(x)=2 to f(x)=4.
Highlight the 1-unit input movement in yellow (#FFD700) and 2-unit output movement in orange (#FFA500).

sections.title: Defining the Local Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: The derivative f'(x) measures local scaling.
It tells how space stretches or squashes.
If the derivative is 3, the space triples.
If it is 0.5, the space compresses.
This view looks at local transformation, not just slope.
animations: Represent the Input Space as a white (#FFFFFF) rubber band with ruler markings.
Stretch the rubber band area around x=2 until it is 3 times its original length.
Label the stretched segment 'f\'(x) = 3 (Local Scaling Factor)' in yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Visualizing f'(x) with Infinitesimal Intervals
lecture_lines: Consider a tiny interval dx in the input.
The function maps dx to a segment df.
The derivative is the ratio of their lengths.
For x squared, segments grow as x increases.
At x equals 3, the output segment is 6-fold.
animations: Zoom in on a small segment 'dx' on the Input Line, colored bright red (#FF0000).
Animate the mapping of 'dx' to a corresponding segment 'df' on the Output Line.
Show 'df' appearing 6 times longer than 'dx' to represent f(x)=x^2 at x=3.
Display the ratio formula f'(x) = df/dx in white (#FFFFFF) next to the segments.
Pulse the 'dx' and 'df' segments to emphasize their relative scaling.

sections.title: The Meaning of Sign and Zero
lecture_lines: A positive derivative preserves the input's direction.
A negative derivative flips the number line's orientation.
A zero derivative collapses local space into one point.
animations: Show a right-pointing arrow moving on the Input Line.
On the Output Line, show a left-pointing arrow to illustrate a negative derivative 'flip'.
Show a segment on the Input Line collapsing to a single point on the Output Line for f'(x)=0.

sections.title: Application: The Stretchy Slime
lecture_lines: Imagine a slime moving through a function field.
Local scaling determines the slime's shape and size.
Where f' is 1, the slime stays normal.
Where f' is 0, the slime is crushed thin.
Negative f' values invert the slime's front and back.
animations: Place the slime [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slime.svg] character blob on the Input Line.
Move the slime [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slime.svg] to x=0; it remains normal size as f'(0)=1.
Move the slime [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slime.svg] to x=π/2; it squashes into a thin vertical line as f'(π/2)=0.
Move the slime [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slime.svg] to x=π; it flips horizontally while maintaining size as f'(π)=-1.
Flash the local scaling values (1, 0, -1) in yellow (#FFFF00) above the slime [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slime.svg] at each point.

sections.title: Summary & Preview of Higher Dimensions
lecture_lines: Derivatives describe how a function reshapes space.
This concept scales to areas and volumes in 3D.
Welcome to the transformational view of calculus.
animations: Show a single grid line being pulled to review the 'Space Stretching' concept.
Transition the line into a 2D grid fabric [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fabric.svg] that warps and stretches in multiple directions.
Display the text 'Next: Jacobians' in light cyan (#E0FFFF) as the 2D grid expands.
